Question: How did trenches on the WW1 western front physically end at their northern and southern terminus?
Answer: I can only speak for the northern, Belgian side. The Belgian army had inundated the front, so they Germans got blocked by a water barrier of the north sea and inundated Yser, which stretched up to Ypres at the British held line. From there the trench lines started. The Southern end stopped at the Swiss border and again at a river, the Rhine near Basel. So it was a clearly defined and strongly held stretch between both rivers.

Question: How do I convert from inches to centimeters and convert back from centimeters to inches in my head quickly?
Answer: I had to convert back and from for many years. But if you think of 4" to be 10 cm, you will be close enough for common use. And 1' is 30 cm, that might help as well. And buy a ruler with both, imperial and metric on it. That will help.
